Sellside Analysts' Memo · Xvivo Perfusion · built 3 November 2026

How the sell-side sees Xvivo Perfusion, and where its view is heading

What each broker on record thinks and how that has moved over twelve months, with the Investment Analyst's judgement on where the sell-side goes next.

  • Three kinds of content, each labelled. The brokers' own commentary, from 29 research reports produced between 7 Jun 2026 and 31 Oct 2026 (blue-edged cards). The Investment Analyst's reading of the sell-side, from its Layers 1 to 4 and three memos (purple-edged cards and the judgement boxes). This memo's summaries, tables and charts, which name their sources.
  • Breadth. 1036 passages from 12 research houses, plus consensus and investor views. Every house the research records on this stock is included, however briefly it appears.
  • Checks. Every quotation was matched word for word to its source by script, every summary sentence was checked against the passages, and every number survived the editing.
How current this is, and what was left out

The research passages come from reports produced between 7 June and 31 October 2026, with DNB Carnegie's and RedEye's dated views reaching back to December 2023 and Morgan Stanley's dated competitor views to May 2019; note titles run from 20 December 2023 to 23 October 2026. The latest broker views are DNB Carnegie's and RedEye's third-quarter reviews of 23 October 2026; the Investment Analyst's Layers 1 and 2 are dated 22 October 2026 and its Layers 3 and 4 and memo 25 October 2026, with the fourth-quarter report named for 28 January 2027.

No passages are flagged as stale April to May 2026 research. Passages on other companies' operations with no read-across stated (for example xenotransplantation and United Therapeutics' facilities) and detailed 2023 to 2025 quarterly beats and misses are used only lightly. The Investment Analyst's 24-month-forward price-to-earnings reading is left out because it rests on a rolling consensus.

The answer in brief

  1. Two Nordic houses carry the debate; four brokers are recorded, all Buy, though passages name others.

    • Four brokers, all Buy: research of 24 October 2026 records four covering brokers (DNB Carnegie, RedEye, Pareto, Stifel), 100 percent Buy ratings; FactSet, read 22 October 2026, shows 100% Buy, unchanged over one, three and six months.
    • Two houses write almost everything: DNB Carnegie and RedEye appear in 426 and 435 of the 1,036 passages; a 24 October 2026 report says The current market narrative is dominated by DNB Carnegie and RedEye.
    • Pareto and Stifel are thin: their SEK 280 and SEK 353 targets come from the Investment Analyst's FactSet data (Layer 1, 22 October 2026), with Buy only inferred from 100 percent Buy ratings; no post-results models surfaced.
    • Highest and lowest targets: Stifel's SEK 353 and Pareto's SEK 280 (both undated); RedEye has scenario values, not a target, and its post-results base case is recorded as SEK 360, 369 or 385 (see conflicts).
    • Context houses are not coverage: Jefferies, Morgan Stanley and Bernstein write on TransMedics, other peers and the sector; Nordea, Rabobank and Intesa Sanpaolo on the Swedish krona. None has an Xvivo rating or target.
    • Also not coverage: Deutsche Bank writes on US hospitals, and Research Capital and Lucid Capital Markets on the United States regulator's process; SEB, Handelsbanken and Danske Bank are only named as covering (see conflicts).
    Source: Research passages; the Investment Analyst's Layer 1 (FactSet); FactSet revisions.

  2. Headlines moved from bruised to recovering, then nervous in July and catalyst-led by October.

    • Twelve months ago, bruised: RedEye's 16 October 2025 preview was headed Still a bit bruised, but breathing; DNB Carnegie's 6 October 2025 preview, Uncertainty remains on EVLP momentum.
    • January 2026, recovery: after fourth-quarter 2025 results on 27 January 2026, DNB Carnegie wrote Q4 indicates strength, not weakness and RedEye Alive and kicking.
    • April to July 2026, steady then nervous: DNB Carnegie's 27 April 2026 title was Growth acceleration and several regulatory catalysts in 2026; on 15 July 2026 RedEye wrote Intact case, nervous stock.
    • July 2026, heart timing: DNB Carnegie's 15 July 2026 review was headed Uncertainties in heart timing, but a strong pulse.
    • Last three months, catalysts: RedEye's 11 August 2026 title read Heart receives CE marking; DNB Carnegie's 7 October title, Share price weakness creates attractive entry; RedEye's 23 October title, Heart opportunity approaching.
    Source: Note titles (ledger).

  3. DNB Carnegie trimmed to SEK 330 in July 2026 and held it; RedEye's post-results scenario values conflict.

    • DNB Carnegie upgraded in July 2025: a table records HOLD / BUY SEK 390 / SEK 330 on 14 July 2025, ending a Hold its ladder shows from April 2024 (Buy-titled notes conflict; see conflicts).
    • DNB Carnegie's target path: SEK 300 (6 October 2025), 295 (21 January 2026), 300 (27 January), 337 (20 April), 340 (27 April) and 330 (15 July 2026), per its ladder in a report of 31 October 2026.
    • DNB Carnegie held after results: its 23 October 2026 review reiterated a buy rating with an unchanged target price of 330.00 Swedish kronor.
    • RedEye's base case conflicts: a 30 October 2026 report says RedEye's 23 October update lowered its DCF-based fair value estimate from SEK 385 to SEK 360; reports of 22 to 31 October give 369 or 385 (scenario values).
    • FactSet target edged down: read on 22 October 2026, the consensus target was SEK 336.14, (3)% over three months; the 18 September mean was SEK 346.14, and the 22 October median SEK 330.00.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; events; the Investment Analyst's readings (18 September and 22 October 2026); FactSet revisions (read 22 October 2026).

  4. The question moved from European heart approval to adoption speed, US timing and the largest customer.

    • From approval to adoption: research of 24 October 2026 says the narrative moved in three months to how fast does Europe adopt and when does the FDA decide.
    • CE mark removed an overhang: a 31 October 2026 report, citing RedEye's 23 October note, says the August 2026 CE mark for the heart device removed a major regulatory overhang.
    • Customer risk took centre stage: DNB Carnegie reported on 23 October 2026 that, despite 32% organic sales growth, the market focused on future customer risks.
    • Margin targets now doubted: RedEye's 23 October 2026 review argued Xvivo will fall short of its 2027 EBITDA target; reports of 21 September and 30 October record RedEye calling the targets achievable (see conflicts).
    • The Investment Analyst's reading: The sell-side's model is a revenue story it believes and a margin story it has been trimming (Layer 1, 22 October 2026).
    Source: Research passages; DNB Carnegie and RedEye; the Investment Analyst's Layer 1.

  5. Both houses expect European heart sales to build in 2027; they differ on when US heart approval comes.

    • RedEye's heart numbers: a report of 31 October 2026 records RedEye projecting that European heart sales will exceed SEK 200 million in 2027e and SEK 500 million in 2028e.
    • DNB Carnegie is lower: DNB Carnegie's 23 October 2026 report expects heart segment sales to reach one hundred eighty million Swedish kronor in 2027; FactSet consensus has SEK 181 million for FY2027 (report of 24 October 2026).
    • Reimbursement takes time: DNB Carnegie's Rolder noted that establishing local reimbursement typically requires twelve months after launch (report of 30 October 2026); RedEye said on 11 August 2026 that France already has full reimbursement.
    • US heart timing differs: DNB Carnegie's base case has FDA approval around mid-2027 (report of 24 October 2026); RedEye (23 October 2026) models approval in late 2027 or early 2028 and a US launch in early 2028.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; FactSet consensus in research.

  6. Both houses size the largest customer's in-house move at 5 to 6 percent of 2027 sales.

    • DNB Carnegie calls fears overdone: its 7 October 2026 preview calculated that Xvivo's exposure was limited to 5% to 6% of its projected 2027 revenue.
    • DNB Carnegie sees margins protected: on 23 October 2026 DNB Carnegie argued that the highest gross margin components will remain in use by Lung Bioengineering.
    • RedEye flags timing noise: RedEye said on 23 October 2026 that the third-quarter beat included SEK 8.5 million of retrospective revenue and SEK 10 million of inventory build-up at the largest US customer.
    • RedEye still sees an offset: a report of 30 October 2026 says RedEye's analysts believe Xvivo is well-positioned to entirely offset the Lung Bioengineering headwind, through adoption at other US centres.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages.

  7. RedEye and DNB Carnegie's October case put 2027 margins below the company's 30 percent goal; other DNB Carnegie passages differ.

    • Consensus below the goal: Consensus expectations sit at 26.80 percent for FY2027 (research of 24 October 2026; 26.8% in the Investment Analyst's Layer 1 of 22 October), against the company's above-30 percent EBITDA target.
    • RedEye at 23 percent: RedEye forecasts a 2027 EBITDA margin of 23% and an EBIT margin of 13%, driven by upfront US launch costs (recorded in a report of 24 October 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie at 26.6 percent: a 22 October 2026 report records DNB Carnegie's October case at 26.6% EBITDA and 17.2% EBIT for 2027; other passages say it assumes above 30% (see conflicts).
    • Services split the houses: RedEye (23 October 2026) calls the (19)% services gross margin a necessary commercial launch infrastructure spend rather than a permanent cash drain; DNB Carnegie (9 October) says it will continue to drain cash.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; consensus passages.

    2027 margins below the company's goal

    Consensus puts the financial year 2027 EBITDA margin at 26.8%, below the company's above-30% target; RedEye forecasts 23%, citing upfront United States launch costs.

  8. FY2027 earnings per share consensus has been cut at every horizon to 22 October 2026: (13)% over twelve months.

    • FY2027 FactSet revisions: earnings per share (5)%, (6)%, (12)% and (13)% over one, three, six and twelve months to 22 October 2026; EBITDA (3)%, (4)%, (7)%, (6)%; sales (1)%, (1)%, (5)%, (5)%.
    • Consensus by year: FactSet medians on 22 October 2026 were SEK 3.38, 6.08, 9.47 and 14.80 for FY2026 to FY2029, down from 3.47, 6.27, 9.61 and 15.15 in the Investment Analyst's 22 September memo.
    • Twelve-month history by year: FY2026 (21.5)%, FY2027 (13.6)% and FY2028 +7.1%; over three months (4.4)%, (5.7)% and (2.7)% (Investment Analyst's Layer 1, 22 October 2026).
    • Momentum turned: the 4 July 2026 memo found Sell-side earnings momentum is strongly positive (score 9); by 22 October The dashboard's revision-momentum score is (10) and its sell-side momentum pin is F.
    • After third-quarter results: on 23 October 2026 DNB Carnegie raised FY2026 adjusted earnings per share 10% to SEK 3.90 and cut FY2027 4% to SEK 5.70 and FY2028 3% to SEK 8.60; RedEye cut 2027 sales 6%.
    Source: FactSet revisions (read 22 October 2026); the Investment Analyst's readings; DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages.

  9. RedEye defends a premium multiple with takeover prices; both main houses value Xvivo by discounted cash flow.

    • Discounted cash flow first: DNB Carnegie's SEK 330 target uses an 8.5% discount rate (report of 31 October 2026); RedEye blends 90% discounted cash flow with 10% peer multiples at 12% (reports of 30 and 31 October).
    • Takeover prices as support: RedEye's 23 October 2026 report argues Getinge's acquisition of Paragonix at eleven times sales and Terumo's purchase of OrganOx at twenty-one times sales support a premium multiple.
    • DNB Carnegie sees value: Rolder notes Xvivo traded at 6.9 times 2026 enterprise value to sales before the results, against peaks of 14 to 16 times in 2022 to 2024 (report of 30 October 2026).
    • RedEye's warning: RedEye notes Xvivo on 44 times 2027 enterprise value to operating profit (23 October 2026), and a report of 24 October records that softer quarters lead to sharp adverse movements.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages.

  10. Investors fixed on the largest customer and short interest; the shares fell despite a third-quarter beat.

    • Beat, then sell-off: RedEye's 22 October 2026 note expected a 5% to 7% share rise on the results, but structural concerns overshadowed the beat (recorded in a report of 25 October 2026).
    • Customer anxiety: RedEye noted on 23 October 2026 that the negative stock reaction reflected deep investor concerns over Lung Bioengineering transitioning to its own platform.
    • Short interest easing: charts in RedEye's 23 October 2026 report show short interest peaking near 12% in April 2026 and falling to about 8.3% by late October; a 25 October report links this to regulatory progress.
    • DNB Carnegie on reactions: after a 10% fall on the second-quarter results day, DNB Carnegie called the drop an overreaction and kept Buy (recorded in a report of 7 August 2026).
    • Share price: SEK 223.40 on 22 October 2026 and SEK 205.0 on 30 October 2026, against a FactSet median target of SEK 330.00 on 22 October 2026.
    Source: RedEye and DNB Carnegie passages on investors; the Investment Analyst's memo.

    The Investment Analyst's verdict

    The Investment Analyst's verdict: the market has priced the known worries into the multiple and not into the numbers.

  11. The Investment Analyst expects FY2027 consensus to be cut again from the fourth-quarter report.

    • Three directions at once: the Investment Analyst (25 October 2026) writes The consensus will move in three directions at once: FY2026 up toward about 3.8, FY2027 down, FY2028 holding or rising toward about 10.5.
    • More FY2027 cuts: the Investment Analyst says From the Q4 2026 report onward I expect FY2027 consensus EPS to be cut; that report is due on 28 January 2027.
    • Buy share at risk: in the Investment Analyst's memo (25 October 2026), the 100 percent Buy share can only move one way, with Pareto's undated SEK 280 target nearest the price.
    • The Investment Analyst's own numbers: FY2027 earnings per share of 3.8 (Layers 3 and 4, 25 October 2026) against the pre-results consensus median of 6.08 (Layer 1, 22 October 2026).
    • Verdict for Richard: For Richard: the market has priced the known worries into the multiple and not into the numbers (Investment Analyst, 25 October 2026).
    Source: The Investment Analyst's Layers 3 and 4 and memo (25 October 2026).

Where the sell-side's view is heading

The Investment Analyst's judgement

The estimate-cutting cycle is part done: the Investment Analyst judges financial year 2027 estimates cut but not capitulated, with a cut likely at each report.

  • Earnings cut, mostly recently: financial year 2027 consensus earnings per share revisions are (13)% over twelve months, (12)% over six, (6)% over three and (5)% over one; EBITDA (6)% and sales (5)% over twelve.
  • Targets and ratings held up: the target price revision is (3)% over three months and one but +1% over six; the Buy share is still 100%, which the Investment Analyst judges has "nowhere to go but down".
  • What turned it: revisions were positive in early July; the second-quarter margin miss brought cuts, from margins and operating costs rather than revenue, on the Investment Analyst's reading; October added the largest customer's step-down.
  • Next, a lift then cuts: the Investment Analyst expects a mechanical lift to financial year 2026 earnings that flatters momentum, then cuts to financial year 2027 at each of the next four reports, a cumulative 25 to 35%.
  • The far year later: the Investment Analyst expects financial year 2028 consensus to hold until the Food and Drug Administration's posture is visible in mid-to-late 2027, then fall 30 to 40%.
  • What would prove it wrong: the Investment Analyst's counter-case, about 10% likely, is a fourth-quarter report with heart sales above 35, lung above 140 and the targets reaffirmed, holding financial year 2027 consensus.
  • What would change the view: for the Investment Analyst, two Tier 2 reimbursement decisions by April 2027 and a regulator's advisory-panel date in the first half of 2027, shrinking the financial year 2027 cuts to one alignment.

What each broker says

Each research house in turn, ordered by how much the research records from it: its view in one line, then how it frames the case, its arguments, its worries and how its view changed. Quoted words are the research report's.

RedEyeOscar Bergman; Richard Ramanius and Lindkvist on some notes; Johan Unnérus in October 2024No price target; scenario values only, conflicting after 23 Oct 2026: base SEK 360, 369 or 385; bear SEK 140 or 145; bull SEK 748 or 785 (reports of 22 to 31 Oct 2026; see conflicts)

RedEye backs Xvivo's long-term heart and liver story but is more cautious than DNB Carnegie on US heart timing and 2027 margins.

Stance and how it got there

  • Base case cut, per one report: a 30 October 2026 report says RedEye's 23 October update cut its base case from SEK 385 to SEK 360, using 90 percent DCF and 10 percent peer-based multiples; others differ.
  • Two scenario sets: reports of 24 and 30 October 2026 give bear SEK 140 and bull SEK 748; reports of 22 and 24 October give bear SEK 145 and bull SEK 785 (see conflicts).
  • Scenario values, not targets: RedEye publishes fair-value scenarios; a table in a 21 September 2026 report records Oscar Bergman on 15 July 2026 as BUY / BUY (Base Case) SEK 385 / SEK 385.

How it frames the case

  • Heart opportunity: RedEye's titles of 13 and 23 October 2026 read Heart opportunity approaches and Heart opportunity approaching.
  • 2028 as the horizon: RedEye's 23 October 2026 review suggested 2028 is the more relevant investment horizon for capturing operational leverage.
  • Thesis intact, stock nervous: RedEye's 15 July 2026 second-quarter review was headed Intact case, nervous stock.

Main arguments

  • European heart sales: RedEye projects European heart sales above SEK 200 million in 2027 and SEK 500 million in 2028 (recorded in a report of 31 October 2026).
  • Customer loss offset: RedEye argued on 23 October 2026 that European heart sales and wider XPS placements will offset the loss; a 24 October report calls it highly likely to be a temporary blip rather than a permanent impairment.
  • Premium multiple justified: RedEye's Bergman cites Getinge's acquisition of Paragonix at 11x EV/Sales and Terumo's acquisition of OrganOx at 21x EV/Sales (report of 30 October 2026).
  • Estimates reshaped: on 23 October 2026 RedEye cut 2027 sales 6% to SEK 1,162 million on lower lung estimates and raised 2028 sales 8% to SEK 1,720 million on higher heart sales.
  • Faster liver route: RedEye says the 510(k) route is faster and cheaper, targeting submission in the first half of 2027 and a US liver launch in early 2028 (report of 24 October 2026).

What worries it

  • US heart timing: RedEye's 23 October 2026 update labels the company's late 2027 launch target as somewhat optimistic, modelling approval in late 2027 or early 2028.
  • 2027 margins: RedEye forecasts a 2027 EBITDA margin of 23% and EBIT margin of 13%, below the company's 30% and 20% targets (report of 24 October 2026).
  • Customer stockpile: RedEye warned on 23 October 2026 that an aggressive transition could mean almost zero consumable orders from this account in early 2027.
  • Services losses: RedEye reported on 22 October 2026 that services sales fell to SEK 14 million and services gross margin to (19)%.
  • Valuation sensitivity: RedEye's 23 October 2026 report highlights Xvivo trading at a demanding 44 times 2027 enterprise value to operating profit.

How its view changed

  • Twelve months: RedEye's tone moved from Still a bit bruised, but breathing (16 October 2025) to Alive and kicking (27 January 2026).
  • Six months: RedEye held its SEK 385 base case from April 2026 through its 13 October preview, while the share price fell.
  • Three months: RedEye welcomed the 11 August 2026 CE mark; on 23 October it moved its US heart launch to early 2028 and, per a 30 October report, cut its base case to SEK 360 (see conflicts).
  • Margin view hardened: a 21 September 2026 report recorded RedEye calling the 2027 targets achievable; by 23 October RedEye expected Xvivo to fall short (see conflicts).

DNB CarnegieElvin Rolder and Maria Karlsson Osipova (2026); Ulrik Trattner named on notes to April 2026Buy, target SEK 330 (reiterated 23 Oct 2026)

DNB Carnegie rates Xvivo Buy at SEK 330, calls customer fears overdone and the liver route a de-risking, while trimming outer-year earnings.

Stance and how it got there

  • Long Hold: DNB Carnegie held Hold from April 2024 to July 2025, arguing that short-term earnings multiples were highly demanding (recorded in a report of 14 July 2026; Buy-titled notes conflict, see conflicts).
  • Upgrade on the fall: DNB Carnegie upgraded to Buy on 14 July 2025, arguing that the sixty percent year-to-date drop created an attractive stock entry point.
  • July 2026 trim: on 15 July 2026 DNB Carnegie cut its target from SEK 340 to SEK 330: Trimmed EBITDA on lower gross margin assumptions if European heart timing shifts.
  • Held after the third quarter: DNB Carnegie reiterated Buy and SEK 330 on 23 October 2026, its title reading Clarity on the route to the US for liver.

How it frames the case

  • Recurring consumables: DNB Carnegie's 7 October 2026 report argues that over 80 percent of Xvivo's revenue comes from recurring consumable sales.
  • Capital-light model: DNB Carnegie says Xvivo's capital-light, stationary OPO placement model provides far more predictable and scalable growth than high-touch national service networks (7 October 2026).
  • Entry point: DNB Carnegie's 7 October 2026 preview was headed Share price weakness creates attractive entry.

Main arguments

  • Customer fears overdone: DNB Carnegie puts the largest customer's in-house move at 5% to 6% of 2027 revenue, with the highest-margin components still bought from Xvivo (7 and 23 October 2026).
  • Liver route de-risks: DNB Carnegie says the 510(k) liver route significantly derisks the cash flow profile compared to a long PMA trial (recorded in a report of 23 October 2026).
  • Valuation attractive: DNB Carnegie's Rolder notes Xvivo previously traded at 14 to 16 times enterprise value to sales in 2022 to 2024 (report of 30 October 2026).
  • Bull case: DNB Carnegie's bull case has 2028 sales of SEK 2.0 billion and a 20 times EBITDA multiple if Xvivo wins large US share (23 October 2026).
  • Clinical edge: DNB Carnegie's Trattner said clinical superiority would let Xvivo take share from TransMedics once its heart and liver systems win US approval (report of 7 August 2026).

What worries it

  • US services gap: DNB Carnegie's 10 March 2026 report says Xvivo's inability to provide necessary transportation and perfusion services in the US market represents a key investment risk.
  • European heart uptake: DNB Carnegie notes that lower-than-expected adoption of XHAT in Europe represents a primary downside risk to forecasts (report of 18 October 2026).
  • Services drain: DNB Carnegie's 9 October 2026 report warns services revenue keeps falling and the segment will drain cash without new procurement contracts.
  • Bear case: DNB Carnegie applies a 25% discount to TransMedics in its bear scenario (recorded in a report of 14 July 2026).
  • Tariffs: DNB Carnegie flags US tariffs on European-made products as a material downside risk to mid-term earnings (report of 24 October 2026).

How its view changed

  • Twelve months: DNB Carnegie cut its target to SEK 300 on 6 October 2025 and, citing SG&A cost ramp-up for regulatory filings, to SEK 295 on 21 January 2026.
  • Six months: DNB Carnegie raised to SEK 340 on 27 April 2026 after the first-quarter beat, then trimmed to SEK 330 on 15 July on gross margin.
  • Three months: after the third quarter DNB Carnegie raised FY2026 earnings per share 10% to SEK 3.90 on tax and financial items, but cut FY2027 to SEK 5.70 and FY2028 to SEK 8.60.
  • US heart timing: a report of 7 August 2026 records DNB Carnegie expecting possible approval by the second half of 2027; a 24 October report records a mid-2027 base case.

JefferiesNo rating or target on Xvivo recorded; its research covers TransMedics

Jefferies' passages concern TransMedics, a United States competitor, and the US transplant market, including expert interviews on Xvivo; they are not a view on Xvivo's shares.

Read-across favourable to Xvivo (not a view on its shares)

  • Expert preference for Xvivo: a Vanderbilt heart transplant cardiologist told Jefferies (24 July 2026) that Xvivo offers comparable outcomes, simpler workflows, and superior economics compared with TransMedics' system.
  • Cost gap: a Jefferies note of 24 July 2026 estimated Xvivo's heart run at about USD 40,000 against about USD 85,000 for TransMedics' system.
  • Market tailwinds: Jefferies notes US pressure on underperforming organ procurement organisations and Medicare reasonable-cost reimbursement as supports for machine perfusion (24 July 2026).

Read-across unfavourable to Xvivo (not a view on its shares)

  • TransMedics entrenched: Jefferies reported on 24 July 2026 that TransMedics took part in 26% of all US thoracic and abdominal transplants in 2025.
  • Trial history: Jefferies noted on 12 October 2025 that Xvivo's cold heart system had previously failed to meet trial endpoints in European clinical settings.
  • Germany slow: a Jefferies note of 5 August 2026 called Germany a more complex market without donation after circulatory death or established reimbursement.
  • OrganOx growth: Jefferies reported in June 2026 that Terumo targets 40% growth for OrganOx; a 24 October 2026 report reads this as more pressure in European liver tenders.

Morgan Stanley's passages concern TransMedics, a United States competitor, plus Terumo, Getinge, the krona and US hospitals, not Xvivo directly.

Read-across from TransMedics (not a view on Xvivo's shares)

  • TransMedics' service moat: Morgan Stanley reported on 9 May 2025 that TransMedics owned 21 aircraft; a report of 25 October 2026 records Morgan Stanley contrasting this with Xvivo's third-party partnerships.
  • Cost strain on centres: Morgan Stanley's 1 October 2024 report said TransMedics' services can total up to USD 110,000 per case, and that cold perfusion was reducing TransMedics' share at major centres.
  • Ramp precedent: Morgan Stanley's 7 November 2023 report showed TransMedics' heart revenue at USD 19 million a quarter eight quarters after approval.

Process, macro and peer points (not a view on Xvivo's shares)

  • Regulatory process: Morgan Stanley wrote on 12 June 2026 that an FDA advisory panel typically extends a review to 320 days from 180, a general process point.
  • Krona and hospitals: Morgan Stanley recommends long Swedish krona positions against the euro (report of 14 July 2026) and its survey shows hospitals capping capital spending (report of 7 August 2026).
  • Deal integration: Morgan Stanley reports that Getinge's Paragonix purchase stays dilutive to adjusted earnings per share until fiscal 2028 (report of 24 October 2026).

Where the brokers disagree

Can Xvivo reach its 2027 margin targets (EBITDA above 30 percent, EBIT above 20 percent)?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie, 7 October 2026: called the 2027 targets realistic and assumed an EBITDA margin above 30% by 2027; a 22 October report puts its October case at 26.6% (see conflicts).
  • RedEye, as recorded: reports of 21 September and 30 October 2026 record RedEye deeming the targets achievable, though dependent on US heart sales.

The more negative side

  • RedEye, 23 October 2026: expects Xvivo to fall short, forecasting a 23% EBITDA margin and 13% EBIT margin for 2027 on US launch costs.
  • DNB Carnegie's October case: 26.6% EBITDA and 17.2% EBIT for 2027, below the targets (report of 22 October 2026).
  • Consensus: 26.8% EBITDA for FY2027 against the 30% target (report of 24 October 2026).

When will Xvivo's heart system be approved and launched in the United States?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie: base case of FDA approval around mid-2027 on a twelve-month review (report of 24 October 2026); in August 2026 it saw possible approval in the second half of 2027.

The more negative side

  • RedEye, 23 October 2026: calls the late-2027 target somewhat optimistic, models approval in late 2027 or early 2028 and moved its US launch to early 2028.
  • Morgan Stanley, 12 June 2026 (general process): an advisory panel referral typically stretches a review to 320 days.

How much will the largest US customer's move to its own lung platform hurt?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie, 7 and 23 October 2026: calls the fears overdone; exposure is 5% to 6% of 2027 revenue and the highest-margin components stay with Xvivo.
  • RedEye, 30 October 2026 report: confident Xvivo can fully offset the loss through other US centres and European heart sales.

The more negative side

  • RedEye, 23 October 2026: an aggressive transition could mean almost no orders from the customer in early 2027; a 30 October report adds that inventory build-up will weigh on fourth-quarter thoracic sales.
  • Investors: RedEye recorded a very negative retail reaction to the customer news on 23 October 2026.

How fast will Europe adopt the heart system after the August 2026 CE mark?

The more positive side

  • RedEye: European heart sales above SEK 200 million in 2027 and SEK 500 million in 2028; a 50% share of Australia's brain-death market is cited as proof (23 October 2026).
  • RedEye, 11 August 2026: France is furthest ahead with full reimbursement in place.

The more negative side

  • DNB Carnegie's Rolder: local reimbursement typically takes twelve months after launch (report of 30 October 2026); Germany's lack of donations makes adoption complex (7 October 2026).
  • RedEye, 11 August 2026: country registrations remain a bottleneck and regional funding is historically slow.
  • Jefferies, 5 August 2026 (market research, not Xvivo coverage): Germany lacks circulatory-death donation and established reimbursement, so it is a slow driver.

Can Xvivo win share from TransMedics in the United States?

The more positive side

  • Jefferies' expert, 24 July 2026 (TransMedics research, not Xvivo coverage): a Vanderbilt cardiologist prefers Xvivo for simpler workflow and better economics; Jefferies puts Xvivo's heart run near USD 40,000 against USD 85,000.
  • DNB Carnegie's Trattner: clinical superiority would win share once heart and liver gain US approval (report of 7 August 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley, 1 October 2024 (TransMedics research, not Xvivo coverage): cold perfusion was already reducing TransMedics' share at major centres.

The more negative side

  • Jefferies, 24 July 2026 (TransMedics research, not Xvivo coverage): TransMedics took part in 26% of US thoracic and abdominal transplants in 2025; on 12 October 2025 it noted Xvivo's heart system had missed European trial endpoints.
  • DNB Carnegie, 10 March 2026: lack of US transport and perfusion services is a key investment risk.
  • Morgan Stanley (TransMedics research, not Xvivo coverage): TransMedics' aviation service is more streamlined than Xvivo's third-party partnerships (report of 25 October 2026).

Is Xvivo's premium multiple justified?

The more positive side

  • RedEye, 23 October 2026: takeovers of Paragonix at 11 times sales and OrganOx at 21 times sales support a premium.
  • DNB Carnegie's Rolder: valuation remains attractive against peaks of 14 to 16 times sales in 2022 to 2024 (report of 30 October 2026).
  • Jefferies, 25 August 2025 (Terumo research, not Xvivo coverage): Terumo's roughly 20 times sales price for OrganOx shows the scarcity value of warm perfusion platforms.

The more negative side

  • RedEye, 23 October 2026: Xvivo trades on 44 times 2027 enterprise value to operating profit, so softer quarters bring sharp share moves.
  • DNB Carnegie: its bear scenario applies a 25% discount to TransMedics (recorded in a report of 14 July 2026).
  • Bernstein, 9 October 2026 (sector, not Xvivo): premium medtech multiples compressed 35% to 65% since late 2024.

Will amortisation and tax dent reported earnings per share?

The more positive side

  • RedEye, 23 October 2026: higher amortisation is non-cash and does not change its SEK 360 base-case scenario value (one of three post-results base cases recorded; see conflicts).
  • DNB Carnegie, 23 October 2026: assumes a 15% paid tax rate through 2028 and raised FY2026 earnings per share on tax effects.

The more negative side

  • Research of 24 October 2026: the SEK 39 million yearly heart amortisation is not fully reflected in consensus models.
  • Tax gap: RedEye assumes a 21% tax rate against DNB Carnegie's 15%; research of 24 October 2026 says aligning tax assumptions would dilute outer-year earnings per share.

Where the research reports conflict. Both versions are shown; this memo does not pick one.
  1. DNB Carnegie recorded as both Buy and Hold in 2024 and 2025.
    • Buy titles: note titles show Buy with targets, for example XVIVO Perfusion (Buy, TP: SEK584.00) on 14 July 2024 and XVIVO Perfusion (Buy, TP: SEK520.00) on 24 April 2025.
    • Hold titles and ladder: titles from the same house read Xvivo (Hold): Growth and operational leverage while risk of earnings volatility on 15 July 2024; its ladder shows Hold from 25 April 2024 to 2 July 2025.
    • Downgrade date unclear: one passage says DNB Carnegie downgraded XVIVO to HOLD in early 2025; others place the Hold from April 2024. The inputs do not explain the two series.
  2. DNB Carnegie's target history differs between passages.
    • Initiation: one passage says DNB Carnegie initiated coverage with a SEK430 target in late 2023; its ladder starts at Buy SEK 350 on 26 January 2024, and a 28 January 2024 title shows SEK 418.
    • 2025 path: one passage records a cut from SEK390 to SEK300 in October 2025; the ladder shows SEK 330 on 14 July 2025 before SEK 300 on 6 October 2025.
    • 2026 direction: one passage says DNB Carnegie raised its target price from SEK295 in January 2026 to SEK330 in October 2026; the ladder shows SEK 340 in April, cut to SEK 330 on 15 July.
    • July 2025 action: one passage says it reiterated its buy rating on 14 July 2025; the table and title record an upgrade from Hold that day.
  3. DNB Carnegie's 2027 margin assumption.
    • Above 30 percent: a 22 October 2026 report says DNB Carnegie expected heavy investment to continue while still assuming a 2027 EBITDA margin above 30% and EBIT margin above 20%; a 7 October passage says the same.
    • Below target: another passage in the same 22 October report says DNB Carnegie's October case remained below that ambition at 26.6% EBITDA and 17.2% EBIT margin for 2027.
    • Not settled: a 23 October passage says the broker's updated model remains more conservative due to expected commercial investments, without giving a number.
  4. RedEye's scenario values after the third quarter.
    • 360, 140 and 748: a report of 30 October 2026 says RedEye cut its base case from SEK 385 to SEK 360 and maintained their long-term bull case of SEK 748 and bear case of SEK 140.
    • 369, 140 and 748: a 24 October 2026 report gives RedEye's October values as a base case at 369 kronor per share and a bull case at 748 kronor, bear 140; a 31 October report also gives 369.
    • 385, 145 and 785: a 22 October 2026 report says RedEye kept these after the results; the 24 October report also lists RedEye's bear 145, base 385 and bull 785 per share, as does the Investment Analyst's Layer 1.
    • Not settled: the inputs do not say which set is current; all are scenario values, not price targets. Reports of June and July 2026 record earlier RedEye scenarios from SEK 165 to SEK 1,150.
  5. RedEye on whether the 2027 margin targets are achievable.
    • Achievable: a 21 September 2026 report says the targets are ones which RedEye deems achievable; a 30 October report records RedEye's analysts deeming them fully achievable targets by 2027.
    • Will fall short: passages on RedEye's 23 October 2026 review say Xvivo will fall short of its 2027 EBITDA target, forecasting 23% EBITDA and 13% EBIT margins.
    • Not settled: the 30 October report post-dates the 23 October review; the inputs do not say which reflects RedEye's current model.
  6. RedEye's recorded rating.
    • Buy: a table in a 21 September 2026 report records RedEye on 15 July 2026 as BUY / BUY (Base Case) SEK 385 / SEK 385.
    • Hold: a 14 July 2026 report, in a passage attributed to RedEye, says the Hold rating was reinforced by a 6-12 month European delay; other passages tie a Hold in that period to DNB Carnegie.
    • Not settled: the inputs do not show which house the Hold passage meant.
  7. Whether RedEye's forecasts include the faster US liver route.
    • Not included: a 22 October 2026 report says RedEye did not incorporate the full benefit into its post-results valuation.
    • Included: a 23 October 2026 report says RedEye's updated estimates incorporate Xvivo's transition to a 510(k) pathway for US liver access.
    • Not settled: the first may describe RedEye's 22 October initial take and the second its 23 October review; the inputs do not say so.
  8. How many houses cover Xvivo.
    • Four: research of 24 October 2026 lists four covering brokers; the Investment Analyst records Four brokers for FY2026 to FY2028, two for FY2029.
    • Two: a 7 June 2026 report refers to the limited two-broker analyst pool.
    • Others named: a 31 October 2026 report says Xvivo is covered by several leading investment banks including SEB, Handelsbanken, Carnegie, and Danske Bank; the 22 September memo counted four named brokers plus one restricted.
  9. The sell-side's response to the third-quarter results.
    • Upgrades: a 31 October 2026 report says Brokers upgraded their medium-term EBITDA and EBIT forecasts following the strong Q3 2026 performance and that analysts upgraded their targets.
    • Holds and cuts: DNB Carnegie kept SEK 330 and cut FY2027 and FY2028 earnings per share 4% and 3%; a 30 October 2026 report says RedEye cut its base-case scenario value from SEK 385 to SEK 360.
    • Not settled: the 31 October passages name no broker.
  10. Date of the FY2027 FactSet mean of 5.81.
    • 16 October: the Investment Analyst's Layers 3 and 4 say the FactSet mean was already 5.81 on 16 October against a 6.08 median.
    • Post-results: the memo calls it FY2027 consensus EPS (5.81 on the post-Q3 FactSet mean); Xvivo reported the third quarter on 22 October 2026.
    • Not settled: the FactSet revisions read on 22 October 2026 also show 5.81; the inputs do not say whether it includes post-results changes.
  11. The sell-side target range.
    • 280 to 353: the Investment Analyst's Layer 1 (22 October 2026) records target prices span 280 (Pareto) to 353 (Stifel) with 100 percent Buy ratings.
    • 280 to 360: the memo of 25 October 2026 says The sell-side's targets (280 to 360) imply 25 to 60 percent upside on their earnings.
    • 310 to 353: the 22 September memo cites targets of 310 to 353 SEK against a 240 SEK price. RedEye's SEK 360 is a scenario value; the memo does not say whether its 360 is that figure.
  12. DNB Carnegie's earnings per share path.
    • Before results: one 22 October 2026 passage says DNB Carnegie had cut to SEK 3.5 for 2026, SEK 6.1 for 2027 and SEK 9.0 for 2028 after Q2; another gives SEK 3.5, 6.0 and 8.9 entering the results.
    • After results: DNB Carnegie moved to SEK 3.90, 5.70 and 8.60 (report of 30 October 2026); another passage says it projects adjusted EPS will rise from SEK 3.86 in 2026 to SEK 8.61 by 2028.
    • Not settled: the differences are small; the inputs do not reconcile them.
